Q0690

“To kill one man is called unrighteousness and incurs one capital crime;…” — Mozi (Mozi, Against Offensive War I)

Verified English quotation. Primary source: Mozi, Against Offensive War I. Theme: justice.

Quotes / Mozi / Q0690

English

To kill one man is called unrighteousness and incurs one capital crime; by this reckoning, to kill ten men is ten times unrighteous and incurs ten capital crimes.
Thinker Mozi
School Mohism
Source Mozi, Against Offensive War I
Theme Justice
Another quotation More from this thinker

About Mozi

Mozi (Mo Di, c. 470–c.

How to read this passage

Distributive, retributive, and restorative justice name different problems. Political philosophy asks what a just society owes its members and outsiders. This passage enters that discussion through justice, morality, ethics.

Concepts in this quote

Justice
Justice concerns fairness, rights, desert, and the arrangement of institutions that claim to treat people as equals.
Morality
Morality in philosophy concerns right and wrong, obligation, and the standards by which we judge persons and acts.
Ethics
Ethics appears in this archive as a live philosophical concern—not a slogan. These verified English passages show how thinkers treat ethics as a problem of judgment, practice, or explanation.
